moves: input: a trader who wants a rule built only from prices already known
rhetorical job: give the motive and the four jobs first, chain the method in one sentence, and route one result to each job
analytical job: compress the screening, the parameter search, the voting rule, the forecast, the terminal values, and the cost finding
output: a reader who knows both terminal values, the margin, and the verdict before any section
handoff: the introduction, which opens with a fragment instead of a number
section_progressions.positive_pattern: motive then roadmap, one chained method sentence, the result sentence reused with new figures, a concession, and a verdict

moves: input: the verdict from the summary, not yet justified
rhetorical job: open with a fragment, build a two-handed tension, and hand the background to a task list
analytical job: fix the three jobs: the strategy and the five-year value, the proof it is best, and the cost sensitivity
output: three tasks, each paired with the method that will answer it
handoff: the work figure, which carries no prose of its own
section_progressions.positive_pattern: a verbless opening, on the one hand and on the other hand, then tasks written as participles

moves: input: the three tasks
rhetorical job: state each assumption as a bare claim and keep the reason on its own line
analytical job: drop the minimum trading unit for both assets and exclude a market-wide crash
output: three assumptions, each justified, with the constraint admitted before it is dropped
handoff: the notation, which shares the page
section_progressions.positive_pattern: number, colon, claim, then a justification that concedes, shrinks, and restates

moves: input: the assumptions
rhetorical job: send the reader to the table in one sentence and define nothing inline
analytical job: collect the symbols used across the models
output: one table of seven symbols
handoff: the model section, which opens on the next page
section_progressions.positive_pattern: one passive sentence that names the table and stops

moves: input: the price series named in the task
rhetorical job: name the cause of the gap before the gap, give the fill, and defend it
analytical job: span the 1826 days and fill the missing gold prices with the previous day
output: a complete price series the factors can be computed on
handoff: the factor selection, which uses only closing prices
section_progressions.positive_pattern: since the cause, there is a lack, for this we use, and the fix will not affect the result

moves: input: the assumptions, the notation, and the filled prices
rhetorical job: grant the common approach and cut it down, sort the factors into families, and gloss each one into a rule
analytical job: define seven factors, search their parameters, build the voting rule, and add the forecast and the stop
output: a voting strategy with tuned parameters, a next-day price, and a forced sale
handoff: the results, which read the figures the search produced
section_progressions.positive_pattern: grant then cut, family sorting, symbol then gloss then rule, and restate the old rule before replacing it

moves: input: the tuned factors and the two strategies
rhetorical job: read every figure as a bullet list and let the margin prove the method
analytical job: report the winning parameters, the trades, and the two terminal values
output: the numbers the optimality section has to defend
handoff: the optimality analysis, which opens on the same page as the comparison
section_progressions.positive_pattern: as the figure can be derived, then the margin and a which-shows clause

moves: input: the reported terminal values and the demand for proof
rhetorical job: defend the factors by common use, build an unreachable ceiling, and concede the bias before claiming the win
analytical job: compare against an omniscient investor and against two named firms
output: a small share of the ceiling and a win over the firms in most years
handoff: the sensitivity section, which changes the cost instead of the benchmark
section_progressions.positive_pattern: commonly used and proven, let's assume an omniscient benchmark, although the comparison favors us

moves: input: the strategy and the commission hidden inside every trade
rhetorical job: sweep the cost, split the factors into two behaviors, and give each behavior its own cause
analytical job: recompute returns and trade counts while the cost runs from nothing to a high rate
output: one behavior that fades and one that holds, and the echoed verdict
handoff: the memorandum, which repeats the verdict for the trader
section_progressions.positive_pattern: cases such as one, while cases such as the other, this is because, and the verdict repeated

moves: input: the whole paper, addressed to a trader who did not read it
rhetorical job: include the reader in the wish, retell the pipeline, point at the rules, and give the result
analytical job: restate the voting sets, the trigger, the four cases, and the terminal value
output: a strategy the trader can follow and a number to judge it by
handoff: nothing follows; the letter closes on a hope and a thanks
section_progressions.positive_pattern: we all want, the strategy is described as follows, we calculated that, and we sincerely hope

main_argument_chains.claim: Seven stock indicators, refit on the first year, give a usable buy rule and sell rule for both assets.
support_steps: grant the habit of judging from outside events, then demote it as only a rough analysis
sort the seven indicators into three families so the list becomes three groups
gloss each one as symbol, plain name, job, and free parameters
turn each gloss into a buy rule and a sell rule joined by conversely
deny that the stock defaults transfer, and search the first year
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Each factor yields a tuned parameter set and a trigger the voting rule can count.

main_argument_chains.claim: A vote of five factors, firing at three or more, plus a next-day forecast and a forced stop, beats the untuned strategy.
support_steps: count the factors that fire and trigger a trade at three or more
route the two-asset case to the mean-variance model
restate the current rule before replacing it, changing only the day the factor is read
justify the stop by a loss reduced and thus a benefit increased
credit the margin to the two additions and close with a bare verdict
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The improved terminal value is the number the rest of the paper defends.

main_argument_chains.claim: The strategy is the best available one, even though an omniscient investor would do far better.
support_steps: defend the factors by common use and by theoretical proof
ask the reader to assume an investor who already knows every future price
report the solver's ceiling and shrink the model's result to a small share of it
concede that the firm comparison drops labor costs the model never pays
claim the higher return only after that concession, and only in most cases
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The recommendation survives a comparison the paper admits is unwinnable and one it admits is biased.

main_argument_chains.claim: Raising the transaction cost trims the result but does not break the strategy.
support_steps: sweep each cost from nothing to a high rate and pick two factors as the types
give the fading factors one cause and the stubborn factors another, joined by while
explain the shared drop with a this-is-because chain ending on the assets
repeat the summary's verdict nearly word for word
repeat it once more in the letter to the trader
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The trader is told the strategy is the stable one, in the same words three times.

warnings.warning: Both EMA lines print a bare C_t. It is not the close w_t and it has no gloss. The skill may write an exponential average of the closing price. It must not copy C_t or treat it as defined.
The left side carries n_1 while the sum is divided by n_2 and runs to n_2-1. The skill may average a smoothed series over its own window. It must not copy the mismatched argument.

The factor (w_i MA_i) is printed with no operator, the sum runs from i=0 to n while dividing by n, and the middle band equals the previous day's average. The skill may write a band around a moving average. It must not copy the missing operator or the limits.

Equation (8) puts the buy flag on the (1-alpha) term and the sell flag on the subtracted term. Equation (10), which claims to unpack it, does the reverse, and equation (25) follows equation (10). The skill may write cash that rises on a sale and falls on a purchase. It must not copy either line as the other's expansion.

Equations (8) and (15) print the trigger as RST with a prime, while equation (13) prints RSI with a prime and the prose says the modified RSI. The skill may name the indicator once. It must not copy the RST spelling or treat the two marks as different indicators.

Equation (7) is the Bollinger formula, not the RSI test the program actually uses. Equations (16) and (17) also print DIF and DEA with no time argument and join the conditions with a bare italic and. The skill may swap one trigger test for another. It must not cite equation (7) as the test being replaced.

The covariance term indexes both weights and the covariance with k, while every other term uses t. The objective is also the square root of its own square, so the minimization has nothing to act on. The skill may minimize a portfolio variance. It must not copy the index or the identity.

Equations (21) and (23) print the activation as the two words tan y, with a space, and equation (22) multiplies the carried cell state by F with no subscript. The skill may write a gated recurrence. It must not copy the spaced activation or the bare F.

Both gold terms are printed x_i with a gd superscript, so the difference is zero and the test can never fire. The bitcoin numerator subtracts x_i rather than the previous day's price the gloss describes, and the gloss adds a stray roman x and a stray roman y. The skill may write a stop at a stated decline. It must not copy equation (24).

The last clause of inner line (6) bounds the sum of the two gold flags by the gold price, mixing a count of flags with a price. The skill may bound a buy flag and a sell flag by one. It must not copy that clause.

model_retention.equation_free_boundary: The voting rule is prose. The count and the trigger at three are never displayed as formulas.
